settings.headline: Make your Senseless Selection
settings.subhead: Within the Senseless System, your selection has two parts — the format, and the strength. Here's how to make it.
settings.image_alt: Senseless Comfort Cream, Comfort Gel and Comfort Spray — the Senseless system

settings.headline: What the Senseless System is
settings.body: Most numbing is one product, sold one way. Senseless is built as a system — three formats and three strengths — so you can match what you use to what you're actually booking. Making your Senseless Selection means two choices, and neither is about buying the most expensive: the format (how it's applied and where) and the strength (how much the session asks for). The rest of this page walks you through both, then a by-procedure guide that puts them together.

settings.headline: Tell us about your appointment.
settings.intro: Three quick answers and we'll point you to the format and strength we'd reach for. A recommendation, not a rule — your practitioner has the final say.

settings.label: Cream
settings.note: Broad coverage, the default for most appointments and larger or simpler areas.

settings.label: Gel
settings.note: Holds exactly where you place it; for precise, facial work and longer sittings.

settings.label: Spray
settings.note: Fast, even, hands-off coverage for large or awkward-to-reach areas.

settings.headline: Selection one: the format
settings.intro: Format is about where the product goes and how it stays there. Three options:
settings.closer: If you're between cream and gel, the question is precision; between cream and spray, it's the size of the area.

settings.matched: The standard. Smaller areas, shorter or routine appointments, and anyone starting out. Fits the majority of sessions.
The higher strength. Larger areas, longer or more sensitive sessions. The one most people settle on for regular work.
The highest in the system. The longest, most demanding, most sustained sessions. More than most appointments need — and we'll tell you when.

settings.headline: Selection two: the strength
settings.body: Strength is separate from format — every format comes in all three. Which you need depends on the session, not the procedure name: how large the area is, how long the appointment runs, how intense it is, and how sensitive your skin is. None is "better" than another; each is built for a different kind of session.
settings.note: Most people don't need the top of the range. Match it to the session you're actually having — if you're between two, the lower one is usually the sensible start, and you can move up next time.
settings.reassurance: Clinical isn't a weaker version of Professional, and Advanced isn't a half-measure. The three are formulated for different sessions, not different levels of quality. Most people are on Clinical or Advanced because that's the right match for their booking — not because they're settling.

settings.notes: Professional is overkill here. Save it.
Many manage without numbing at all — optional, not required.
Clinical is rarely enough on its own.
Cream for the face; spray for the body.
The area decides the format and the strength.

settings.recommendation: Gel, Advanced · Professional for long sittings
settings.notes: Clinical rarely enough for a full sitting.
Spray covers large zones fast and evenly.
Cream for lip, brow and small areas.

settings.headline: Putting your selection together: what we recommend by procedure
settings.body: The honest version — the format and strength we'd point you to for each treatment, what's overkill, and what's rarely enough. This is a guide, so it covers injectables too; on the shop pages we keep those separate.
settings.closer: If you're between strengths, choose the higher one — the cost of going up is small; the cost of going too low for an intensive session is real.

settings.heading: Before you buy: a word most sellers skip
settings.body: For a lot of treatments the practitioner applies their own numbing as standard — microneedling especially. If yours does, you may not need to bring your own, and turning up already numbed without checking can get in the way. Self-applied numbing matters most where the practitioner doesn't provide it, or where you want extra preparation on top. A quick message before you book settles it.

settings.headline: The system in four lines
settings.body:
• Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range by Matrix Health Group Ltd — not a medicine.

settings.question: What's the difference between Clinical, Advanced and Professional?
settings.answer: Different strengths of the same range. Clinical is the standard for routine sessions, Advanced is higher for longer or more sensitive work, Professional is the highest for the most demanding appointments.

settings.question: Is the strongest one always best?
settings.answer: No. Matching the strength to the appointment matters more than reaching for the highest — for many treatments the top strength is more than you need.

settings.question: How do I choose between cream, gel and spray?
settings.answer: Cream for broad coverage and most appointments, gel for precise facial work that needs to stay put, spray for large or awkward-to-reach areas.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product, not a medicine.
